request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Case 3 presented with chronic sinusitis, hyperglycemia, difficulty in breathing, fever, dry cough, general body weakness, and 72% oximetry saturation. He was subsequently diagnosed with COVID-19.

Hospital Course:
The patient was isolated and taken to a designated isolation center for treatment and monitoring. He received supportive therapy for his symptoms.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up:
The patient is advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider for further evaluation and management of his symptoms. He is also advised to take appropriate precautions to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient will be discharged home with instructions to continue self-isolation and monitor his symptoms. He is advised to seek further medical attention if his symptoms worsen or if he develops new symptoms. The patient is also advised to follow all public health guidelines to prevent the spread of COVID-19. 

Summary:
Case 3, a 40-year-old male, presented with chronic sinusitis, hyperglycemia, difficulty in breathing, and fever. He was subsequently diagnosed with COVID-19 and received supportive therapy during his hospitalization. The patient will be discharged home with instructions to continue self-isolation and monitor his symptoms. He is advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider and to take appropriate precautions to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 is coded U07.1 (virus identified) or U07.2 (clinically diagnosed). The presentation here includes hypoxia with 72% saturation, difficulty breathing, fever and cough, and the diagnosis was COVID-19. The question asks for a letter and two digits, and the instructions list chapters without U. U07 is the special-purpose code for COVID-19 in ICD-10-AM (Chapter 22). The listed chapters are only examples, so U07 is a valid answer.

If COVID-19 pneumonia were documented, the code would still be U07.1 with J12.82. Here pneumonia is not documented, and the principal diagnosis is COVID-19, so U07.

CODE: U07
